description: Test files that exist in this repository and are NOT executed by the pull-request gate. Every entry is a hole in what a green pull request means, stated so that a reader of that green knows what it does not cover. `unrun` is EMPTY at this head, and that is a statement rather than an omission: the tier it used to declare is now executed and governed. The `governed` block below records what closed it, so the file goes on being the place a reader looks.
whyThisFileExists: apps/web/playwright.config.ts gates tests/e2e/authenticated/** behind ROOTLCO_E2E_AUTH === '1'. For the whole of P1-27 no workflow set it, so the repository's ONLY end-to-end tenant-isolation proof and its ONLY route-level accessibility proof had never once executed anywhere but on the Owner's machine, while `test:web-e2e` reported a green browser tier and the phase records counted browser coverage. Nothing said so anywhere. This file, the LOUD job-summary step in .github/workflows/_reusable-node-quality.yml that reads it, and tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts are what replaced that silence.
whatChangedAndWhatDidNot: TWO changes, a phase apart. FIRST the tier was WIRED: a job stood the Supabase stack up with the vendored CLI, bootstrapped the real operator and the second tenant through scripts/dev/owner-acceptance/create-owner-account.mjs, started the production API build as a database login holding neither SUPERUSER nor BYPASSRLS, ran `npm run test:web-e2e-authenticated` with ROOTLCO_E2E_AUTH=1, and FAILED unless every authenticated spec file contributed at least one executed test. The earlier claim recorded here — that a hosted runner cannot be given a live Supabase, a live API and a real account — was false: a hosted runner has Docker and the Supabase CLI is a devDependency of this repository. SECOND, and this is what emptied `unrun`, the tier became GOVERNED: the job body moved to .github/workflows/_reusable-authenticated-browser.yml, both `pr-ci.yml` and `protected-develop-verification.yml` call it, `authenticated-browser` is in DECLARED_JOBS in scripts/ci/evaluate-ci-gate.mjs, and it is in the `needs` of both `ci-gate` and `protected-gate`. Neither gate can report Go while this check is red. What did NOT change is the strength of the tier itself: the same specs, the same zero-test guard.
hostedObservation: OBSERVED SIX TIMES, and the last three PASSED. Recorded run by run, because a single sentence about this tier has already been wrong twice in this phase — first claiming a hosted runner could not stand the stack up, then claiming the tier had never executed. Both were checked against the GitHub API rather than against this file, which is how they were caught. (1) Run 31337158296, workflow_dispatch on remediation/p1-27-final-canonical-blockers, commit 155a5f55fdd5b6262ea2ed9c421dcf98f5bc83a7, job 93304793606: FAILED. supabase start, supabase:reset across every migration and seed, the identity-provider settings, /auth/v1/health, the Playwright install and all five acceptance identities each succeeded; the bootstrap then failed at scripts/dev/owner-acceptance/create-owner-account.mjs, because alignLocalJwtSigning recreates the GoTrue container (docker rm -f then docker run -d) and assertHs256 probed the token endpoint once with no retry — the recreate returned at 21:38:21.029 and the probe failed with 502 ten milliseconds later. A readiness race in the acceptance bootstrap, not the algorithm refusal its error text blamed, and not a limitation of hosted CI. ZERO tests executed; the zero-test guard failed the run rather than reporting green. (2) Run 31343632011, commit 0c40499be0a6a42dc984436437ffff9d90d45e5d, job 93321402511: FAILED, and this is the first time this tier ever produced test results anywhere but the Owner machine — 212 passed, 11 failed. The readiness race was gone (align-local-jwt.mjs now retries for 30 s on 502/503/504 and ECONNREFUSED only). The eleven were real product and test defects: seven isolation assertions that had begun measuring the loading skeleton rather than the rendered page, two planted accessibility violations, and two duplicate queues issuing no POST. (3) Run 31347643485, commit 78c458723671ac1c7d7c8721a09d4fd156283054, job 93332452247: PASSED. 229 tests planned, 225 passed, 0 failed, 224 executed across all 6 spec files in 3.2 minutes. The job conclusion is success. NOTE that the RUN conclusion is failure — other jobs in that workflow were red at that commit — which is exactly why this file, the gate and the workflow all read the per-job conclusion on the commit and never the run-level one. (4) Run 31508526699, commit 424e5d884ed7c8f608c446408743cbf88ac80515, job 93836261616: PASSED. 229 tests planned, 225 passed, 0 failed, 224 executed across all 6 spec files in 3.1 minutes. THIS IS THE CLOSING CANDIDATE. It is the run P1-27-QA-005 seals against, and it supersedes run 31347643485 as the evidence any current claim about this tier must cite — that run measured 78c4587, which is not the commit this phase closes on. WHAT IS AND IS NOT SETTLED. Settled: this tier runs on a hosted runner, and has passed there. SETTLED at the closing candidate by run (4): the tier has been observed to pass on the commit this phase closes on, with authenticated-browser sitting in the needs of both ci-gate and protected-gate. The earlier caveat on this field — that no run had been observed at the closing candidate — is discharged, and is kept here in the record rather than deleted, because it was true for three of the four runs above. (5) THE SEVENTH SPEC WAS NOT YET OBSERVED ON A HOSTED RUNNER WHEN THIS PARAGRAPH WAS WRITTEN, and it is kept in the past tense it now belongs to rather than deleted, because it was the honest statement for runs (1) through (4). `governed.specs` names SEVEN files; every run recorded above measured SIX. `apps/web/tests/e2e/authenticated/appointments-and-receptions.spec.ts` did not exist at 424e5d884ed7c8f608c446408743cbf88ac80515, the commit run (4) measured, so "224 executed across all 6 spec files" is a true and complete statement about the tier as it then stood and is NOT a statement about the tier this file now declares. The paragraph also recorded a LOCAL execution on the acceptance stack — a live Supabase, a production `next build` of apps/api serving on 3000, and `next start` serving apps/web on 3210 — stated with the same numbers a hosted one would carry so that it could be compared against run (6) when run (6) existed: 315 planned, 310 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped, 8.5 minutes, across all SEVEN spec files; 146 in `authenticated-en`, 145 in `authenticated-ar`, 18 in `authenticated-tablet` and the `auth-setup` sign-in; the seventh spec contributed 43 executed cases in each of the two locale projects and skipped none. The five skips are `accessibility.spec.ts` cases that need a customer and a vehicle to exist and pre-date this branch. A developer machine is not the governed runner: a local pass is the reason to expect the hosted one and never a substitute for it. The paragraph's own instruction was that the first `authenticated-browser` run on this branch be recorded as run (6) with its id, its commit and its counts, exactly as (1) through (4) were. (6) Run 31750364479, `pull_request` on feature/p1-28-appointment-vehicle-reception-frontend for PR #226, commit 38afa5c28e5b78d484a442cf6b8596fb2a5c34aa, job 94614564003: PASSED, per-job conclusion success in 11m 37s. 370 planned, 366 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped, 0 flaky, across all SEVEN spec files. THE SEVENTH SPEC IS COVERED, which is what this paragraph was waiting for: `authenticated/appointments-and-receptions.spec.ts` contributed 141 cases — 47 in `authenticated-en`, 47 in `authenticated-ar` and 47 in `authenticated-tablet`, 0 failed and 0 skipped — read per test entry out of the run's own playwright-report.json and grouped by `projectName`, not inferred from a keyword count. The tablet figure is new and is not a re-count of run (4): `apps/web/playwright.config.ts:255` widened the `authenticated-tablet` project's `testMatch` to `(administration|appointments-and-receptions)` after that run, so this is the first hosted execution of any P1-28 screen at 1024x768. The four skips are two cases each of `accessibility.spec.ts` under the two locale projects; one of the five local skips is gone because the local run and this one stood different fixtures up, and no P1-28 case is skipped in either. The whole run's 21 checks are recorded in docs/phase-1/phase-1-28/evidence/closure-candidate.json, and `build-p1-28-evidence-manifest.mjs` refuses this field if it goes back to saying the seventh spec is unobserved while a run at the CURRENT candidate stands. RUN (6) NOW DESCRIBES A SUPERSEDED HEAD, and the sentences above are kept in the past tense they belong to rather than deleted. Three fix waves changed 37 product files after 38afa5c28e5b78d484a442cf6b8596fb2a5c34aa, so P1-28-QA-005 re-froze its candidate at 6392ccb4321b004ed12e5d04ad583298da3303dd and every hosted figure taken from run 31750364479 is recorded there as PENDING at that candidate, marked `describesSupersededHead`, and listed in `pendingHostedBindings`. What run (6) settles is unchanged and is not withdrawn: this tier runs on a hosted runner, it has passed there, and the seventh spec HAS executed on one. What it does not settle is the current candidate, and no run has yet been taken at it. Record that run here as (7), with its id, its commit and its counts, exactly as (1) through (6) were. WHAT REMAINS UNPAID: an execution at the current closing candidate, and an execution on a PROTECTED ref. Runs (1) through (6) are all pull-request or dispatch runs; `protected-develop-verification.yml` calls the same reusable job on every push to develop and main, and that observation exists only after PR #226 merges.
policy: An entry in `unrun` is a debt, not a dispensation. It must name what the pull-request gate does not prove, why that job does not run it, which job does, what remains unrepaid, what compensates today, and a date by which the arrangement is revisited. tests/ci/e2e-tier-coverage.test.ts fails when a spec is neither executed by a gate-governed job nor declared here, when a declared spec IS executed by the pull-request gate (a declaration must not be able to hide a runnable tier), when a field is missing, when the named executing job does not exist in the workflow it names, and when reviewBy has passed. It also fails in the OTHER direction: while the tier is governed, an entry may not be re-added here — a debt must not outlive its repayment.
howToClose: CLOSED. Both steps of the recorded plan were carried out. The job was added to DECLARED_JOBS in scripts/ci/evaluate-ci-gate.mjs and to the `needs` of both `protected-gate` and `ci-gate`, which required the job to exist in pr-ci.yml as well — done by moving the body into a reusable workflow called from both — and therefore required the job counts in docs/engineering/ci-automation/pull-request-body.md to be updated in the same commit, which they were, derived from the workflows rather than typed. A passing hosted execution HAS since been observed — run 31347643485, job 93332452247, 225 passed and 0 failed. See `hostedObservation` for all six runs, one by one. What is still owed is not an execution but an execution AT THE CLOSING CANDIDATE: every observed run predates the merge of the five remediation branches, and QA-005 is the measurement that seals the tier against the final head. Governing the check before it had ever gone green was the correct order, and it remains correct now for a different reason — the gate refuses a merge whose candidate this tier has not been run against.

governed.since: 415a869d72141cbab5ee2079cdae695e232ecdc9 — the commit that added .github/workflows/_reusable-authenticated-browser.yml and put the job in both gates. Named as a sha because every sibling field names a checkable artefact and a description is not one: a reader could not verify the previous wording without first reconstructing the search it describes.
governed.executedBy: .github/workflows/_reusable-authenticated-browser.yml job `authenticated-browser`, called by `pr-ci.yml` (same-repository pull requests only) and by `protected-develop-verification.yml` (every push to develop and main, and before a merge by workflow_dispatch pinned to a candidate-sha).
governed.governedBy: `ci-gate` in pr-ci.yml and `protected-gate` in protected-develop-verification.yml. Both list `authenticated-browser` in `needs`; `scripts/ci/evaluate-ci-gate.mjs` declares it `alwaysRequired` and refuses to accept a skip of it unless the caller states `--trusted-context false`, in which case the state is reported as `NOT_ELIGIBLE_FOR_SECURITY_REASON` and never as a pass.
governed.forkPolicy: A pull request from a fork does NOT receive this job: it stands a full Supabase stack, a production API and a real operator account up on the runner, and untrusted code must not be given privileged execution. The gate is told so explicitly and records the refusal; it does not infer it from the absence of a result.
